title: Live proof: a small real PRD from repository to release, surviving a forced crash mid-write
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04). EPIC-FINAL integration-and-hardening row (get_context.isEpicFinal); the ONLY row of this epic that carries dependsOn - the owner chose this explicitly on 2026-09-04 as the single exception to 'tasks should be full and not depended on other tasks', so the runtime withholds it until every feature row is DONE.

VISION 'Next major milestone': 'Give Moe a small but real PRD. Moe asks the necessary questions, creates the architecture and UX, builds the complete application, launches a working preview, proves every requirement, survives a forced crash, and prepares a production-ready release.' Stage 1 bar (proposed, 2026-08-22): the crash lands MID-WRITE and recovery is provable from durable records alone, never from agent memory.

DELIVERABLE: run the whole loop on a FRESH product from the browser only, with real seats, and record it: New product from PRD (bootstrapped repository) -> Activate project -> Gate 1 with at least one real clarification -> Design -> plan -> nodes built in parallel to 100% criteria coverage -> working preview approved (Gate 2) -> release PR opened with the dossier (Gate 3) -> PREVIEW environment deployed with migrations and environment variables -> health probes UP. During one node's landing, kill the daemon process mid-write (a fault-injection knob the daemon already carries or this row adds under a DEVELOPMENT_ONLY flag), restart it, and prove recovery from the store alone: the landing is either COMMITTED exactly once or REFUSED with a code - never duplicated, never lost. Every criterion in the dossier is VERIFIED at the released sha.

ALSO OWNS (rails: the verification budget concentrates in the epic-final row): the whole-epic regression across every lane including the per-package apps/** runs; the docs sweep (README 'What runs today' and 'What this is not' rewritten to the measured state with its date, VISION roadmap status lines, runbook covering every new kind); the adversarial pass over the epic's new human-only kinds (each MCP-excluded, each refusal code reachable); and the follow-up items the feature rows recorded in their comments.

THE PRD: small but real - e.g. a 3-screen TypeScript web app with sign-in, one PostgreSQL table and one API; the human supplies or approves it at claim time (comment on this row). Dogfood note: Moe shipping its own pull request on moe-next remains the harder dogfood (VISION); this row's proof is the fresh product, not moe-next itself.
definitionOfDone: Transcript of the full browser-only run on a fresh product recorded as a row comment series (each under 4500 chars): bootstrap receipt, activation witness, Gate 1 decision id + the clarification, design ref, plan run id, node landing shas (at least 2 nodes, at least 2 staffed concurrently), preview receipt + decision, release receipt + PR URL, deploy receipt + health URL, migration receipt, environment fingerprints.

Forced crash mid-write: the daemon is killed during a landing write (knob name + timestamp recorded); after restart the ledger shows exactly one outcome for that landing (COMMITTED once or REFUSED with its code) and the goal resumes; the recovery evidence is a store query quoted with its result, not a log line.
The release dossier at the released sha shows every approved criterion VERIFIED (n/n) and is attached to the opened PR (URL in the comment).

Whole-epic regression green with count lines quoted: `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, `pnpm test:integration` (from PowerShell), `pnpm test:security`, `pnpm test:property`.
README 'What runs today' + 'What this is not' rewritten to the measured 'as of <date>' state; VISION Stage 1 / Stage 2 status lines updated; the runbook covers every kind this epic added.

Adversarial pass comment: a table of every human-only kind added by this epic -> its MCP refusal code -> the test file:line that pins it; every follow-up item recorded in the feature rows' comments is either closed here or listed with a reason.
taskRails: FEATURES ONLY (human DoD 2026-09-04): no security-boundary or policy work in this row. The verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace v0.1 limitation; signing, hermetic verification and freeze manifests are out of scope.

EVIDENCE, NEVER FABRICATION (epic rail 4 + global rails): every claim in the transcript names its measurement anchor (store path, sha, receipt id); a gate that prints no count line did not run; a live step that refuses is recorded verbatim and the row goes BLOCKED with blockedOnTaskIds or a comment - never a narrowed DoD.

PROVE IT LIVE: the run is a fresh product directory (not UnAI's existing store) driven from the browser only; the seeds/scripts under scratchpad are not used for any step the product claims to do itself. Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat (claim TTL 30 min, memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

REUSE THE EXISTING CRASH MACHINERY FIRST: tests/e2e/foundation/j3-crash-harness.ts and j3-crash-recovery.e2e.test.ts already kill and restart a real daemon and assert recovery, and dispatch-crash-sweep.e2e.test.ts sweeps dispatch crashes — read them before inventing a mechanism, and say in the step note whether the knob is new or an extension of theirs.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 — THE FAULT-INJECTION KNOB. NEW, not an extension. worker-bcaa6d5e, 2026-09-08/09.

THE STEP ASKED ME TO SAY WHETHER IT IS NEW OR AN EXTENSION OF THE EXISTING HARNESSES. NEW, and the reason is structural, not preference. tests/e2e/foundation/j3-crash-harness.ts kills a daemon EXTERNALLY (`killPid` from j1-loop-harness), and dispatch-crash-sweep does the same for dispatch. An external kill cannot aim at the window this row has to prove: the gap between the git commit and the journal completion that records it is microseconds wide and has no externally observable edge. Only the process itself can die there. So the knob is in-process; it composes with those harnesses (they restart and replay) rather than replacing them.

WHERE THE WINDOW IS — measured by reading node-lander.ts:225-260 and node-lander-journal.ts, not assumed. The landing write is: recordRepositoryLandingIntent -> startRepositoryLandingAttempt -> port.commit (THE GIT EFFECT) -> recordRepositoryLandingCompletion -> back in node-lander, recordLandingReceipt. Die after port.commit and the repo has a commit no durable record names; on restart landOne sees no receipt and would re-land. That is exactly "never duplicated, never lost", and landingJournalGate:11 is what closes it (REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED).

- node-lander-journal.ts (MODIFIED, 52 lines) — four fault.trip() calls, plus optional `fault` input for test injection.

THE FENCES, and why they are shaped this way
- OFF unless MOE_FAULT_INJECT_LANDING names a point. Absent/blank -> FAULT_INJECTION_DISARMED.
- REFUSES unless MOE_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY is EXACTLY "1". "true"/"yes"/"1 "/" 1"/"0" all refuse. A loose parser here is a denial-of-service switch in a normal run.
- THE DEVELOPMENT FENCE ANSWERS FIRST. An unknown point name outside development reads NOT_DEVELOPMENT, never POINT_UNKNOWN — an unarmed caller learns nothing about which names exist. Global rail 1 says name WHICH layer refused when two could; the order is asserted, not commented.
- SIGKILL via process.kill(process.pid,"SIGKILL"), not process.exit: an exit runs handlers, flushes and closes the store, which is a graceful shutdown, and recovering from one proves nothing. The knob-name+timestamp note goes out with a synchronous writeSync(2,...) BEFORE the signal, because nothing after it flushes — that is DoD 2's "knob name + timestamp recorded".
- The module header says plainly it is NOT a security boundary: anyone who can set this daemon's env can start a different daemon. The fences are correctness (cannot fire by accident), not a threat model. Task rail 1 keeps security work out of scope and I did not smuggle any in.

ROSTER COVERAGE IS BIDIRECTIONAL (global rail 9). node-lander-journal-fault.test.ts drives a REAL store+handle (recoveryEvidenceFixture) and collects every point the write actually trips, then asserts set-equality against LANDING_FAULT_POINTS in both directions plus order. Iterating the roster alone would stay green if a trip call were deleted. HONEST LIMIT: the legacy no-handle composition trips only before-intent and after-commit — there is no intent or completion to sit between. Direction 2 still holds there; the set-equality arm is on the handle path, which is production.

implementationPlan.description: THE BROWSER-ONLY RUN ON A FRESH PRODUCT (DoD 1). A FRESH product directory — NOT UnAI's existing store (task rail 3) — driven from the browser only, with real seats. The scripts under scratchpad are not used for ANY step the product claims to do itself; using one to bootstrap the repository would make the bootstrap claim false. Walk the whole loop and record each artefact as a row comment in a series, EACH UNDER 4500 CHARS (comments truncate silently at 5000, so a 6000-char transcript loses its tail without saying so): bootstrap receipt, activation witness, Gate 1 decision id AND the real clarification (DoD 1 requires at least one — if the PRD is unambiguous enough that the seat asks nothing, that is a finding to record, not a step to fake), design ref, plan run id, node landing shas for at least 2 nodes with at least 2 STAFFED CONCURRENTLY (the multi-node feature this epic built), preview receipt + decision, release receipt + PR URL, deploy receipt + health URL, migration receipt, environment fingerprints. Every claim names its measurement anchor — store path, sha, receipt id (task rail 2). NEVER RESTART THE WRAPPER to unstick a seat: the claim TTL is 30 minutes and a restart just waits a full lease.

THE CRASH, MID-WRITE (DoD 2 — the Stage 1 bar, and the hardest claim in this row). Kill the daemon DURING a landing write, recording the knob name and the timestamp. Then restart and prove recovery FROM THE STORE ALONE, never from agent memory or a log line: the ledger shows EXACTLY ONE outcome for that landing — COMMITTED once, or REFUSED with its code — never duplicated and never lost, and the goal resumes. THE EVIDENCE IS A STORE QUERY QUOTED WITH ITS RESULT (DoD 2 says so explicitly); a log line saying 'recovered' is not evidence, because the log is written by the process whose correctness is in question. Assert the ONE-OUTCOME property by counting rows for that landing in the durable ledger, not by observing that the goal looks fine afterwards — a duplicate landing also looks fine.

THE RELEASE DOSSIER AT THE RELEASED SHA (DoD 3). Every approved criterion reads VERIFIED, n/n, in the dossier AT the released sha, and the dossier is attached to the opened PR with its URL in the comment. Assert the fraction with its DENOMINATOR — 'all verified' without n/n hides a dossier that enumerated fewer criteria than the contract approved, which is the failure mode this clause exists to catch. Cross-check the criterion COUNT against the approved Product Contract revision rather than against the dossier's own header, since a dossier that dropped a criterion would report itself complete.

WHOLE-EPIC REGRESSION (DoD 4). Every leg standalone and foreground, each `Test Files N passed` count line quoted VERBATIM; a leg that prints no count line DID NOT RUN and must not be reported as a pass (global rail 8, and task rail 2 repeats it). The DoD names: `pnpm test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, `pnpm test:integration` (from PowerShell), `pnpm test:security`, `pnpm test:property`. State explicitly that `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** (global rail 18), so the two --filter legs are what cover the daemon and control room. ALSO RUN `pnpm test:fault` and quote it: the repo has that lane (tests/fault, `test:fault` in package.json) and this row ADDS A CRASH KNOB — the DoD's list predates that decision and omitting the fault lane while shipping fault-injection would be the obvious gap. If it is red for reasons this row did not cause, attribute by the merge-base/HEAD delta and disclose it verbatim (global rail 3).

THE DOCS SWEEP (DoD 5). README's 'What runs today' and 'What this is not' rewritten to the MEASURED state with its date — 'as of <date>' — and that date must be the date of the run in step 3, not the date of writing. The 'What this is not' section exists to be honest about gaps: anything this epic did NOT close stays listed, and anything it did close comes out with evidence behind it. Update the VISION Stage 1 / Stage 2 status lines. The runbook covers every kind this epic added — enumerate them from the epic's DONE rows rather than from memory, or a kind shipped by a row you did not personally plan will be missed. Cross-check against the clauses sibling rows already rewrote (the multi-node row rewrote README's 'one node at a time' sentence; the Gate 2 row rewrote 'no working preview') so this sweep does not reintroduce a claim they retired.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS AND THE FOLLOW-UP LEDGER (DoD 6), as a row comment. (a) A TABLE: every human-only kind this epic added -> its MCP refusal code -> the test file:line that PINS it. Build the kind list from the epic's DONE rows, and for each one open the named test and confirm the pin is real — a table entry citing a line that does not assert the refusal is worse than an empty table, because it retires the question while answering nothing (global rail 4). (b) Every follow-up item recorded in the feature rows' comments (collected in step 1) is either CLOSED here with evidence, or listed with the reason it is not — no silent drops. (c) The integration-level adversarial read across the whole epic: what happens when the crash lands during a PREVIEW rather than a landing; whether any human-only kind became reachable over MCP through a path added late in the epic; and whether the concurrency the multi-node work introduced can interleave two landings on one goal. Where an answer is 'not covered', list it in (b) rather than opening a new row — this IS the epic's hardening row (global rail 21).
